# ARM3 root instruction — same winner-shape prompt as ARM2, 31B base

Schedule and limits follow the public Flexonafft V10 bundle shape, Apache-2.0,
restated here in our own words and adapted to our envelope of 28 tool calls,
8 minutes, 80 turns. Lines marked ARM come from our own 0/21 autopsy, not
from V10.

Mission: You are an autonomous software engineer. Your job is to make the
smallest correct change to SOURCE code under /workspace so the hidden tests
for the issue pass. Hidden tests were written from the issue text, so exact
names, messages, types and behaviors in the issue are the specification.

## STEP 1 — SPEC, zero tool calls

From the issue write three lines in thinking. TRIGGER is the input or action
that causes the bug. EXPECTED is the exact output, value, message or behavior
wanted. ACCEPTANCE is the check that would prove it fixed. Every later step
must serve ACCEPTANCE.

## HARD LIMITS

- 28 tool calls and 8 minutes total. When either runs out, the tree is graded
  as is. An edit that exists counts even with no submit_patch call. An
  unedited tree always scores zero.
- Never create, modify or delete test files. That means files whose names
  start with test followed by underscore, files whose names end with
  underscore test dot py, and anything under tests, test or testing dirs.
  Automatic failure.
- Never run a full suite. No bare pytest, no pytest dot, no unittest
  discover. Always name ONE test file, and add -k when you can.
- Never look outside /workspace. All deps are preinstalled. No pip, no
  downloads.
- Never call the three graph tools search_similar_code, get_code_neighbors,
  get_code_subgraph. They return nothing useful. All nine tools stay
  declared, but these three are banned by this prompt.
- ARM: never rewrite a whole file with write_file. A 99KB spray scored zero.
  Small edit_file blocks only, and read plus or minus 40 lines around a hit
  before editing, never whole files.
- ARM: never touch packaging or config: conftest.py, pytest.ini,
  pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py,
  or any pth file.
- ARM: never re-edit the same hunk without a test run between. Second touch
  on one site means stop, run the issue test, then decide.

## CALL PLAN

- Calls 1 to 8: locate and read. Pull exact symbol names from STEP 1, grep
  -rn for them, read around the hits. Batch independent calls in one block.
  End with a ranked top-3 file list in thinking. No source edit before that
  list exists.
- Calls 9 to 12: edit. You MUST have edited a source file by call 12.
  Unsure: best-guess edit in the most likely place now. A wrong edit can be
  corrected. Pure reading cannot score.
- Calls 13 to 20: verify and correct. Run ONE test file with -k for the
  issue behavior. Fix, rerun. Mirror the fix across sync and async variants
  where the bug lives in shared logic.
- Call 20 onward: no new exploration. git diff, fix, submit.
- Always finish with git diff followed by submit_patch. submit_patch is free
  and ends the loop after this turn.

## VERIFY, before any submit

- Run the issue-shaped test only: the exact request, output, redirect or
  message from the issue. A passing unrelated file proves nothing and has
  scored zero repeatedly.
- Byte-compile changed files: python3 -m py_compile on each changed py
  file. Fix any FAIL, never submit with one.
- git status short and git diff stat: confirm only intended source files
  changed. Delete any scratch under /workspace.
- Traceback-backward rule: when a command fails, the next action navigates
  from that traceback import chain, never a fresh broad search.

## EVIDENCE LINE, ARM calibration asset, zero calls

Final text ends with exactly one line of the form CONFIDENCE number BECAUSE
quoted line, with number from 0.00 to 1.00. QUOTE means copy a
tool-returned line character for character: an exit code line, an OK or FAIL
line, a PASS count. Paraphrase is confabulation. No quoted evidence means
keep working. Never submit an empty or untested patch: both score zero.

Problem Statement:
Handle unusual __qualname__ in inspect

<!--
Please note that Rich isn't accepting any new features at this point.

If a feature can be implemented without modifying the core library, then
they should be released as a third-party module. I can accept updates to the
core library that make it easier to extend (think hooks).

Bugfixes are always welcome of course.

Sometimes it is not clear what is a feature and what is a bug fix.
If there is any doubt, please open a discussion first.

-->

<!--
*Are you contributing typo fixes?*

If your PR solely consists of typos, at least one must be in the docs to warrant an addition to CONTRIBUTORS.md
-->

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation / docstrings
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate (see note about typos above).
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

The user is reporting a bug in `rich.inspect` where an object with a non-string `__qualname__` causes it to fail.
The example provided is:
```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect

@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install
    install()
    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```
The issue is that `__qualname__` might not be a string.

TRIGGER: Calling `inspect()` on an object (or an object that has a non-string `__qualname__` attribute, or when `inspect` tries to access `__qualname__` of an object).
EXPECTED: `inspect` should handle non-string `__qualname__` gracefully, perhaps falling back to `__name__` or another fallback.
ACCEPTANCE: The provided example code should run without failing.

Let's start by reproducing the issue.

Let's look at `_get_signature` again:

The line `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` could be the problem if `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` returns something that is not a string.
Then `Text.assemble` is called with `qualname`.
`Text.assemble` expects strings or `Text` objects. If `qualname` is a `member_descriptor` (as seen in the reproduction output), it might fail.

Wait, the reproduction output showed:
```
Testing inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)...
╭──────────────── <class 'member_descriptor'> ─────────────────╮
│ ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │
│ │ <member '__qualname__' of 'Klaas' objects>               │ │
│ ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ │
```
This was `inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)`. In this case, `obj` is the `member_descriptor`.
`_get_signature` is called if `callable(obj)`. Is a `member_descriptor` callable?
No, usually not.

Wait, the failure happened at `inspect(Klaas, all=True)`.
In this case, `obj` is `Klaas`.
`Klaas` is a class, so `callable(obj)` is True.
`_get_signature("", Klaas)` is called.
Inside `_get_signature("", Klaas)`:
`name` is `""`.
`qualname = "" or getattr(Klaas, "__qualname__", "")`.
`Klaas` has `__slots__ = ("__qualname__",)`.
Wait, if `Klaas` is decorated with `@lru_cache`, what happens?
The example says:
```python

class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)
```
`lru_cache` on a class is unusual. `lru_cache` is typically for functions.
If you decorate a class with `lru_cache`, the class itself becomes the result of `lru_cache`.
Actually, `lru_cache` returns a wrapper.

Let's see what `Klaas.__qualname__` is in the reproduction script.
The output of `inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)` showed `<class 'member_descriptor'>`.
So `Klaas.__qualname__` is a `member_descriptor`.

`obj` is `Klaas`.
`_get_signature("", Klaas)` is called.
`qualname = "" or getattr(Klaas, "__qualname__", "")`.
Since `Klaas.__qualname__` is a `member_descriptor`, `qualname` becomes that `member_descriptor`.
Then `Text.assemble` is called:

`Text.assemble` will try to use `qualname` as a string. If it's a `member_descriptor`, it might fail.

steps.message:
Confirmed. `Text.assemble` fails when `qualname` is not a string or `Text`.

The fix suggested in the issue is:
"I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback."

So in `_get_signature`, I should change:
`qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)`
to something that ensures `qualname` is a string.

Let's see how to implement this.
If `name` is provided (not empty), use it.
If not, try `__qualname__`. If `__qualname__` is a string, use it.
If not, try `__name__`. If `__name__` is a string, use it.
Otherwise, use `name` (which is `""` in this case).

Wait, the original code was:
`qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)`

If `name` is `""`, it does `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", "")`.
If `obj.__qualname__` is a `member_descriptor`, `qualname` becomes a `member_descriptor`.

Proposed fix:
```python
        qualname = name
        if not qualname:
            qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
            if not isinstance(qualname, str):
                qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
                if not isinstance(qualname, str):
                    qualname = name
```
Wait, if `name` is `""`, and `getattr(obj, "__name__", "")` also returns something not a string, it will end up as `""`.

Let's refine this.
```python
        qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
            if not isinstance(qualname, str):
                qualname = name
```
Wait, if `name` is `""`, and `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", "")` is a `member_descriptor`, then `qualname` is a `member_descriptor`.
Then `isinstance(qualname, str)` is False.
Then `qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", "")`.
If `obj.__name__` is a string, we are good.
If `obj.__name__` is also not a string, then `qualname = name` (which is `""`).

This seems to match the description.

Let's check where this is in `rich/_inspect.py`.
It's in `_get_signature` method.

```python
    def _get_signature(self, name: str, obj: Any) -> Optional[Text]:
        # ...
        signature_text = self.highlighter(_signature)

        qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)

        # If obj is a module, there may be classes (which are callable) to display
```

I will apply this change.

Wait, I should also check if there are other places where `__qualname__` is used similarly.
I saw `get_object_types_mro_as_strings` also uses `__qualname__`.

```python
def get_object_types_mro_as_strings(obj: object) -> Collection[str]:
    """
    Returns the MRO of an object's class as full qualified names, or of the object itself if it's a class.

    Examples:
        `object_types_mro_as_strings(JSONDecoder)` will return `['json.decoder.JSONDecoder', 'builtins.object']`
    """
    return [
        f'{getattr(type_, "__module__", "")}.{getattr(type_, "__qualname__", "")}'
        for type_ in get_object_types_mro(obj)
    ]
```
Here it's used in an f-string: `f'{...}.{getattr(type_, "__qualname__", "")}'`.
F-strings call `__str__` on the object, so it won't fail with a `TypeError` like `Text.assemble` does. It will just print the `repr` of the `member_descriptor`.
However, the issue specifically mentioned `inspect` failing.

Let's check if `get_object_types_mro_as_strings` should also be fixed.
The issue says "an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail."
`get_object_types_mro_as_strings` is used by `is_object_one_of_types`.
If `__qualname__` is a descriptor, `f'{...}.{getattr(type_, "__qualname__", "")}'` will produce something like `module.<member '__qualname__' of 'Klaas' objects>`.
This might not be what's intended, but it won't crash.

The crash is definitely in `_get_signature`.

Let's double check the fix.
```python

        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)

```
If `name` is `"my_func"`, `qualname` becomes `"my_func"`. `isinstance("my_func", str)` is True. Correct.
If `name` is `""`, `qualname` becomes `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", "")`.
If `obj.__qualname__` is `"MyClass.my_method"`, `qualname` is `"MyClass.my_method"`. `isinstance` is True. Correct.
If `obj.__qualname__` is a `member_descriptor`, `qualname` is a `member_descriptor`. `isinstance` is False.
Then `qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", "")`.
If `obj.__name__` is `"my_method"`, `qualname` is `"my_method"`. `isinstance` is True. Correct.
If `obj.__name__` is also a `member_descriptor`, `qualname` is a `member_descriptor`. `isinstance` is False.
Then `qualname = name` (which is `""`). Correct.

Wait, what if `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` returns `None`?
`isinstance(None, str)` is False.
Then it tries `__name__`. If that's `None`, it uses `name`.
This seems robust.

The issue says "an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail."

It's used in `is_object_one_of_types`.
```python
def is_object_one_of_types(
    obj: object, fully_qualified_types_names: Collection[str]
) -> bool:
    """
    Returns `True` if the given object's class (or the object itself, if it's a class) has one of the
    fully qualified names in its MRO.
    """
    for type_name in get_object_types_mro_as_strings(obj):
        if type_name in fully_qualified_types_names:
            return True
    return False
```
